issues.description: The problem statement and the template/solution disagree on the Farm API/ method signatures for printing the song. The UML and task text ask students to implement printFarmSong() (and the UML shows a private singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void), but the template and solution expose a public singFarmSong() method instead of printFarmSong(), and the template's private singFarmSongVerse currently has no Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out). This mismatch in method name/signature can confuse students about which method to implement and prevent them from following the UML/task description directly.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the API consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() as the public method that plays the song (and keep singFarmSongVerse(Animal) as the private helper), or (B) rename the template/solution method to printFarmSong() (public) and ensure the private singFarmSongVerse signature includes the Animal parameter. Also, in the template, restore the Animal parameter on singFarmSongVerse (e.g. private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so students can implement the verse printing according to the UML and the provided solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task description) refers to a method named printFarmSong(), but the template and solution use a public method named singFarmSong() (and Main calls farm.singFarmSong()). This mismatch can mislead students: the instruction asks them to implement printFarmSong(), which does not exist in the starter code, while the actual starter API and reference solution expose singFarmSong().
issues.suggested_fix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() (recommended, since the template, Main, and solution already use that name), or (B) rename the public singFarmSong() method in the template and solution to printFarmSong() and adjust Main accordingly. Prefer option A to minimize changes to code examples.
